q: The polynomial method in circuit complexity (Razborov-Smolensky) uses the fact that any depth-d AC⁰[p] circuit (with MOD-p for prime p) computing a function f can be approximated by a polynomial of degree:
opts: O(n^{1/d}) with probability 1−1/n over random restrictions
exp: Razborov-Smolensky: AC⁰[p] circuits of size S and depth d have degree O(log S · log(1/ε))^d approximating polynomials over GF(p). For constant d and S = poly(n), the approximating polynomial has degree O(log^d n). This shows MOD_q (q≠p prime) requires exponential-size AC⁰[p] circuits.
